sentences.text:
3. Heard Sri P.Trivikram Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for home representing learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents.
4. The detenu was detained on the ground that he was involved in six property offences.

Out of these six property offences, he confessed committing of crime in four cases and accordingly, he was convicted and sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment/Simple Imprisonment for four months and the period of remand was set off.
Having regard to this development, the detaining authority assumes that there is every possibility of detenu applying for bail in the remaining two crimes and being released on bail.
Assuming that if the detenu is released there is every possibility of detenu resorting to committing similar crimes and such conduct would affect the public order, the order of detention is passed.
5. Admittedly, the crimes registered against the detenu concern theft of motor vehicles.
Merely because the detenu is involved in six crimes of theft of motor cycles, cannot be a ground to take an extreme measure of preventive detention.

The crimes alleged against the detenu are ordinary criminal cases which can be prosecuted in the normal course of enforcement of law and order and do not warrant resort to extreme measure of preventively detaining the detenu.
The order of detention is liable to be set aside.

6. The impugned detention order passed by the Office of the Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad City -2nd respondent vide SB (I) No.95/PD-2/HYD/2021 dated 29.04.2021 and the consequential confirmation order of the Principal Secretary to Government, General Administration (SPL.(Law &
Order) Department, Secretariat, Hyderabad-1st respondent confirming the detention vide G.O.Rt.No.1452, General Administration (SPL.(Law & Order) Department dated 06.07.2021, are hereby set aside and the Writ Petition is allowed.
